title: How do we add two Roman numerals without changing them?
description: Two Roman numerals are added by counting the symbols of each kind and swapping every full group for a bigger symbol. The video does this for the numerals for 232 and 413, and checks the sum with our own numbers. Keeko's doubt is that the symbols can stay in one long row.
teaching_notes: One idea: to add Roman numerals, gather the same symbols and then swap every full group for a bigger symbol. Start with the smallest symbols and work upwards. Watch for students who leave five of one symbol in the answer.

source: Add CCXXXII and CCCCXIII without converting them to Hindu nu
video_script.why: The child sees that Roman numerals can be added by gathering the symbols and regrouping, with no need to change them to our numerals.
video_script.substitution: Count each kind of symbol in both numerals, then swap every full group for the next bigger symbol, starting from the smallest.
video_script.anchor: the two Roman numerals CCXXXII and CCCCXIII written one above the other
video_script.wrong_answer: keep six see, four ex and five eye in one long row
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko leaves six C, four X and five I in one long row. A row with five I or five C still holds full groups that can become a bigger symbol.
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is dee see ex el vee

final_answer.spoken: dee see ex el vee, which is six hundred forty five

never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: count the symbols: C's 2 + 4 = 6, X's 3 + 1 = 4, I's 2 + 3 = 5
4 X's are written XL, 10 less than 50
6 C's: 5 C's make a D and 1 C is left, so DC
the sum is DC, XL and V together: DCXLV = 500 + 100 + 40 + 5 = 645
video_script.design: One idea: gather the same symbols, then swap every full group for a bigger one. The two numerals stay on the stage and their symbols slide into piles.

<bookmark mark='nums'/>Here are the Roman numerals for two hundred thirty two and four hundred thirteen.

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, count the symbols of each kind.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Two see and four see make six see.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three ex and one ex make four ex.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two eye and three eye make five eye.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: five I's make one V

marks.m4: the five I symbols are circled and swapped for one V

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, start with the small symbols.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Five eye make one vee, so we swap the five eye for one vee.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: four X's are written XL, ten less than fifty

marks.m5: the four X symbols are replaced by an X placed before an L, with a note that 40 is 10 less than 50

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, look at the four ex.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Four ex are written as ex el, because forty is ten less than fifty.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: six C's: five C's make a D, one C is left, so DC

marks.m6: five of the six C symbols are circled and swapped for one D, and one C is left
marks.m7: the D and the left over C are written together as DC

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, look at the six see.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>Five see make one dee, and one see is left.
<bookmark mark='m7'/>Six see are written dee see.

marks.res: the symbols of the answer add back to 645

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The sum is dee see ex el vee.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check with our numbers. Two hundred thirty two plus four hundred thirteen makes six hundred forty five.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Dee see ex el vee is five hundred, one hundred, forty and five. That also makes six hundred forty five.
